```{r}
#Load the dataset
library(datasetsICR)
data(customers)
summary(customers)
```
# Convert categorical variables to factors (categorical)
```{r}
customers$Channel <- as.factor(customers$Channel)
```

## First and Last observations
```{r}
head(customers, 10)
tail(customers, 10)
```
## structure of the Dataset
```{r}
str(customers)
```
## Summary statistics for Fresh and Milk
```{r}
#Fresh and Milk variables
sum_fresh <- summary(customers$Fresh)
sum_milk  <- summary(customers$Milk)

list(
  Fresh = sum_fresh,
  Milk  = sum_milk
)
```
## Create a table for the factor (categorical) variable 
```{r}
library(knitr)
library(kableExtra)
customers$Channel <- as.factor(customers$Channel)

channel_table <- table(customers$Channel)

kable(
  as.data.frame(channel_table),
  col.names = c("Channel", "Frequency"),
  caption = "Customer distribution by channel"
)
# ChatGPT (OpenAI) assisted only with table formatting
```
## Developing different versions of charts
## Option 1
```{r}
library(ggplot2)
ggplot(customers, aes(x = Fresh, y = Milk)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.7) +
  labs(
    title = "Fresh vs Milk Spending (All Customers)",
    x = "Fresh product spending (Fresh)",
    y = "Milk product spending (Milk)"
  )

```
## Option 2 - Fresh
```{r}
ggplot(customers, aes(x = Channel, y = Fresh)) +
  stat_summary(fun = mean, geom = "col") +
  labs(
    title = "Average Fresh Spending by Channel",
    x = "Channel",
    y = "Average Fresh spending"
  )

```
## Option 3 - Milk
```{r}
ggplot(customers, aes(x = Channel, y = Milk)) +
  stat_summary(fun = mean, geom = "col") +
  labs(
    title = "Average Milk Spending by Channel",
    x = "Channel",
    y = "Average Milk spending"
  )

```

## Final chart 
```{r}
customers$Channel <- factor(
  customers$Channel,
  levels = c(1, 2),
  labels = c("Horeca", "Retail")
)

ggplot(customers, aes(x = Fresh, y = Milk, color = Channel)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.7) +
  labs(
    title = "Fresh vs Milk Spending by Customer Channel",
    subtitle = "Each point represents one customer",
    x = "Fresh spending (Fresh)",
    y = "Milk spending (Milk)",
    color = "Customer Channel",
    caption = "Source: customers dataset (datasetsICR package)"
  )


# ChatGPT (OpenAI) assisted only with presentation choices (scales and labels)
```

## Data interpretation {.small-text}
There is a clear positive relationship between Fresh and Milk spending. Customers who spend more on Fresh products generally also spend more on Milk products.

Spending behavior differs by customer Channel. Horeca and Retail customers show different spending patterns, which suggests that customer type influences how products are purchased.

Most customers concentrate at lower to moderate spending levels, while a small number of customers show much higher spending. These high-spending customers appear as visible outliers in the chart, even without using log-scaled axes.

## Recomendations: {.small-text}
Based on feedback from my classmates, I made several changes to improve the clarity and readability of the analysis. The original charts were seen as too complex, so I removed log-scaled axes and smoothing lines to make the numbers easier to understand.

I also added clearer titles, axis labels, and legends so it is easy to identify which variables represent Fresh and Milk spending. The final chart focuses on a simple and direct comparison that can be understood at a quick glance.

Overall, these changes helped make the visualizations cleaner, easier to read, and more effective in communicating the main insights to a general audience.
